newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals seek clearer direction.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals seek clearer direction.

text.p: Precious metals dealers were looking for a more settled direction in their markets on Friday after two days of whipsaw movements.
Silver led the way up on Thursday on speculative buying after the dollar slipped against the yen, bringing losses on the stock and bond markets.
But the silver rally, which was driven by the investment funds, began to lose its way on Friday morning due to gold's inability to match it, dealers said.
"Silver hit a brick wall when it got no encouragement from gold. It's been a bit disappointing," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $378.35 per ounce compared with $378.60 on Thursday afternoon and a London close of $379.20/$379.70.
"There has been no obvious direction this week, with selling one day and buying the next. We need a good close to set the market up positively for next week," a dealer said.
That would mean ending the Europe trading day above $380.00, with an equivalent level registered on the Comex December futures contract, the dealer said.
Producer selling from Australia in "significant" volume kept gold's attempts to rise capped in Asia. "But if it can overcome that selling, it could move higher," a dealer said.

The mini-revival in precious metals was sparked when the bull trend of the dollar against the yen stalled on comments by the head of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Financial Bureau, Eisuke Sakakibara, who said the Ministry was not trying to push the yen lower.
The dollar was still under 112 yen in Europe on Friday morning having closed on Wednesday at 113.90 yen.
Silver was indicated at $4.83/$4.865 at 1045 GMT, a couple of cents off its European opening but still four cents up on Thursday's close.
"The (U.S.) funds were the buyers yesterday and there was some short covering, but Europe did more of the selling and was caught a bit on the hop," one dealer said.
He added that a falure by silver to close above $4.90 could be taken as a signal to start selling again.
"It could head back lower. The $4.75 is pivotal. If it gets down there again we could see $4.60," the dealer said.
Silver briefly traded at a fresh 18-month low of $4.72 on Wednesday.
Platinum and palladium were steady at $382.00/$383.00 and $116.75/$117.75, down five cents and up 75 cents respectively.
